title: one-point etale splitting and strict decrease of isolated fibre points
statement: Let R→S be a finite-type map of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and p a prime. If the set of points of Spec(κ(p)⊗_R S) [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-affine-spectrum] with open singleton has positive finite cardinality, there exist an étale R-algebra R₁ [def-weil-etale-morphism], a prime P over p with bijective canonical residue-field map, and R₁-algebras A,D with D finite type, C=R₁⊗_R S≅A×D and A finite as R₁-module, such that the isolated-point set in Spec(κ(P)⊗_{R₁}D) has strictly smaller cardinality than that in Spec(κ(p)⊗_R S). No assertion that the remaining fibre has no isolated points is made.

proof.text: Choose an isolated fibre point from the positive ncard. Apply the inverse of PrimeSpectrum.preimageHomeomorphFiber to obtain a prime q over p. Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt.of_isOpen_singleton on the fibre, followed by of_quasiFiniteAt_residueField, establishes Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R q. These are the fibre correspondence and quasi-finiteness facts recorded by the cited nodes.
Apply Algebra.exists_etale_isIdempotentElem_forall_liesOver_eq (00UJ) to q. It gives R₁, P, e, r, residue-field bijectivity and finiteness of C[e⁻¹], where C=R₁⊗[R]S.

Construct A=C/(1-e) and D=C/(e), using their actual quotient rings. Mathlib IsLocalization.Away.quotient_of_isIdempotentElem identifies A as C[e⁻¹]; the localization algebra equivalence transfers module finiteness. AlgEquiv.prodQuotientOfIsIdempotentElem with 1-e and e supplies C≃A×D. D is finite type as a quotient of the base change. These are direct applications of the indicated Mathlib declarations, not choices of unproved existence witnesses.
Apply the complementary-fibre cardinal lemma to e, q and r, with their supplied contraction, avoidance and residue-field data. This supplies the strict decrease, completing the one-point removal.
